scenarios.draft: Verify that an admin user can successfully retrieve a paginated list of all guest session records. The test should ensure that the response contains expected guest metadata (session token, IP, timestamps). Data should include both recent and historical sessions. Only admin-level authenticated requests are permitted; attempts by non-admins or guests should be rejected by RBAC, though such negative scenarios may rely on excluded endpoints for dependency. Error scenarios should verify database connectivity handling and appropriate error responses for infrastructure failure.

Test advanced filtering and searching for guest session records. As an admin user, submit various filter queries (by IP, session token fragment, or date range) and verify the paginated, filtered results match the query. Ensure that correct results are returned for expected filter cases (e.g., a specific guest IP). Also confirm that invalid queries (e.g., malformed date ranges or non-existent session token fragments) result in proper error messages, not system failures.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple guest sessions with varying IPs and session tokens so that filtering can be accurately tested for different values.

scenarios.draft: Verify that an admin can fetch full details for a single guest access session record via its guestId. The response should contain all relevant fields, including IP address, session token, and timestamps. Attempting to access a non-existent guestId should return a 404 error. Attempted access by non-admin roles should result in an authorization error (RBAC negative test), though execution of such a path may be in dependency. Confirm that proper validation and error handling occur for malformed or unauthorized requests.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new guest session so the returned guestId can be used to fetch details for a real record.

scenarios.draft: Verify that a new guest session can be registered with valid IP address, unique session token, and timestamp. Confirm that after successful creation, the response contains all expected data (including guestId and timestamps), and that session records are persisted for future audit purposes. Attempt to register two sessions with the same token should not fail unless additional uniqueness rules are present. Error scenarios should test missing/invalid required fields (e.g., invalid IP, null session token), and ensure that blocked or excessive abuse attempts (rate limiting) are handled according to business policy.

Verify that as an admin, it's possible to update details on a registered guest session record (IP address, session token, or entry timestamp). The test should confirm that after updating, the record reflects the new values, and that audit logs (if accessible elsewhere) record the update. Attempt to update a non-existent guestId and confirm a 404 error is returned. Provide an invalid value for a field (e.g., non-IP string for IP address) and verify appropriate validation error. Ensure permission error is returned if attempted by a non-admin.

dependencies.purpose: Register a guest session record which can be updated as part of the admin session update test.

scenarios.draft: Test the ability of a moderator user to search and filter moderation reports using different filter criteria such as reporter identity, content type, report status, category, date range, and related post/comment IDs. Verify that expected pagination, sorting, and fields are returned, and that role-based access control is enforced. Confirm that filters return only accessible reports and pagination metadata is correct. Include dependency on at least one content report being present (either by prior creation or as a prerequisite of test).

dependencies.purpose: Ensure at least one content report exists in the system for meaningful search and filtering operations.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin user can execute advanced searches for moderation/abuse reports, applying various combinations of filters (reporter identity, report status, category, referenced post or comment, date range) and pagination/sort settings. Confirm that returned data matches filter expectations, pagination metadata is correct, and only accessible reports are returned. Validate proper role-based access, error responses for invalid queries, and results aligning with complex audit and triage cases. Ensure prerequisite content reports are present in the system.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure there are moderation reports available in the database before executing the search/filter tests.

scenarios.draft: Test that a moderator can retrieve full detail for a specific content moderation report by ID, including all critical business and audit fields (report reason, reporter, related post or comment, status, timestamps, etc.). Confirm that proper error responses (404 not found, 403 forbidden) are returned if the report does not exist or is not accessible to the moderator. Confirm RBAC enforcement and that data matches record in the database. Requires a known content report ID present in the system.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new content moderation report to fetch its details, ensuring a valid ID for the test.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can retrieve complete business and audit details for a specific moderation/content abuse report by its unique ID. Confirm that fields such as reporter, target, reason, status, category, and audit timestamps are included. Validate correct error behavior for missing or unauthorized access, and that RBAC is enforced. Dependency on having at least one moderation report present, created if needed via content report creation.

dependencies.purpose: Create a content report in the system for which the admin can fetch details and verify data accuracy.

scenarios.draft: Test that a logged-in member can create a new content moderation (abuse) report for a given post or comment, specifying the appropriate reason, category, content reference (postId or commentId), and optional details. Confirm that the system validates referenced content, requires mandatory fields, and logs the event. On success, the created report should return full audit information. Requires that the post or comment to be reported already exist.

Attempt to create a moderation report referencing a non-existent or already deleted post/comment as a member. Verify that the system returns an appropriate error indicating missing content and does not create the report. Confirms validation of foreign key references on abuse reporting APIs.

Attempt to submit a content report as a member with missing mandatory fields such as content reference, reason, or category. Verify that the API enforces required fields and returns descriptive validation error responses, preventing incomplete submissions.

Simulate a guest reporting abusive content using this endpoint (if permitted by business logic), and confirm guest identity is extracted from session, not the payload. Results should show successful submission or appropriate restriction based on endpoint role configuration.

Verify the ability of a moderator to search and paginate the moderation actions record using different filtering criteria such as action type, actor (admin or moderator), report reference, and date range. Scenario should include filtering for a specific type of moderation action (e.g., 'suspend' or 'delete'), as well as negative cases (e.g., searching with no matching result, wrong actor id). Pagination and sorting should be covered. Moderator must have proper authentication. Error scenarios: invalid filter criteria, unauthorized user access, and exceeding page size limits.

dependencies.purpose: Create several moderation actions with different types and actors to populate the dataset for search and filtering.
Generate content reports to be referenced by moderation actions, ensuring realistic report-action linkage for filter testing.

scenarios.draft: Verify that an admin can retrieve the full details of a specific moderation action by its unique id. Test with a valid moderationActionId to ensure all relevant information (type, actor, report reference, rationale, timestamp) is returned. Also test error scenarios: access with an invalid or non-existing moderationActionId (expect 404), and request by an unauthorized role (expect 403 or similar permission error).

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderation action as an admin to ensure there is a valid record to retrieve in the main test.

scenarios.draft: Ensure a moderator can access the full details of a specific moderation action using a valid ID. Test successful data retrieval, and failure scenarios such as invalid or unauthorized access: attempt retrieval with an incorrect id (expect 404), as well as as a user without appropriate permissions (expect 403/unauthorized).

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderation action as a moderator to have a valid moderationActionId for evaluation.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can successfully create a new moderation action in response to a content report, using valid input data (including actor, action type, report reference, and rationale). Confirm the record is persisted and returned with all relevant metadata. Also test duplicate or repeat attempts for the same report-action combination (may expect uniqueness handling or allow multiples per business logic). Error scenarios should include missing required fields, reference to non-existing content report, invalid role/actor, or malformed rationale.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new content report to serve as the reference for the moderation action under test.

scenarios.draft: Validate that a moderator can submit a new moderation action for an associated content report, supplying all required fields (action type, report reference, rationale, etc.) and that the record is created and audit-logged correctly. The scenario also covers attempts with missing or invalid data: omitting required fields, referencing an invalid or deleted content report, or providing an invalid actor. Check that the API enforces RBAC by denying creation by unauthorized roles. Success is verified by the action's existence and its relationships to the actor and report.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new content report as a prerequisite for associating a moderation action in the test.

scenarios.draft: Test searching and filtering guest notifications with various criteria (category, status, type, date range). First, create a guest session using the appropriate endpoint to obtain a guestId and initiate the audit trail. Generate several notifications for that guest using the notification creation endpoint, varying the notification category, status (read/unread), and creation timestamps. Then, as the guest, apply different filter parameters (e.g., unread only, notifications of a particular category, or those delivered within a certain period) and ensure the results match the applied filters precisely, are paginated correctly, and that notifications for other users (members, admins, etc.) are not returned. Verify that unauthorized filter attempts or malformed queries yield validation errors.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new guest session to obtain a guestId for the notification context.
Create notification records associated with the generated guest session for subsequent searching and filtering.

scenarios.draft: Test detail retrieval of an individual notification for an admin user. First, create an admin account and authenticate. Create a notification that explicitly targets this admin using the notification creation endpoint. Then, attempt to fetch this notification by its ID as the correct admin. Validate that all details are returned as per the schema. Additionally, attempt to fetch a notification belonging to another user (member/moderator/guest) to verify that access is denied (forbidden or not found). Ensure all error messages are clear and roles are strictly enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin account for testing notification ownership and detail retrieval.
Create notification records linked to the admin account for detail view and permission validation.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving the detail of a single notification as a moderator. First, set up a moderator account and create at least one notification specifically for that moderator. As the moderator, retrieve the notification by its ID and confirm all fields match what was sent. Additionally, attempt to access a notification addressed to another user (admin, member, or guest) and check that access is denied or results in not found. This scenario also covers attempts to access nonexistent notifications for robust error handling.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderator account to receive notifications.
Create notifications scoped for the moderator to support retrieval and permission tests.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a notification detail as a member user. Begin by creating a member account and generating at least one notification addressed directly to that member. As the member, request the notification's details using the notificationId and verify the schema and that notification contents are accurate. Additionally, test attempts to access notifications belonging to other members, admins, moderators, or guests, confirming that such requests are denied or result in appropriate error responses. Attempt to fetch a notification using a random invalid ID to validate error handling of non-existent records.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member account to own and receive notifications.
Create notifications addressed to the member for subsequent retrieval and permission checking.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving the details of a notification for a guest user. Create a guest session and then deliver one or more notifications to that guest. Using the provided notificationId, attempt to get the notification's full details and verify data fidelity. Also, test attempts to retrieve notifications not belonging to the guest—such as those of members, admins, or other guests—forbidden or not found results are expected. Finally, ensure that attempts to fetch notifications for expired/invalid session tokens or non-existent notificationIds are handled properly with suitable error responses.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new guest session for notification assignment.
Deliver notifications to the guest session for retrieval and access control validation.

scenarios.draft: Test successful creation of a new audit log entry by an authenticated admin. This involves triggering a valid moderation or system event, collecting the related action reference, actor identity (admin), action_type, context, and a valid timestamp. Submit the request and verify the returned audit log record contains all fields and is immutable after creation.

dependencies.purpose: First, create a moderation action event so an action reference can legitimately be supplied for the audit log creation.

scenarios.draft: Test the system's behavior when attempting to create a duplicate audit log entry with the same action reference and timestamp as an existing record. Should return an error or prevent duplication per compliance policy.

dependencies.purpose: First, create a valid audit log entry to intentionally create a conflict condition to test for duplication handling.

scenarios.draft: Test failure when the given action reference does not exist or is not permitted (e.g., wrong UUID, deleted action). Submission should reject invalid references and clarify the error response.

Test the ability for an admin to edit a mutable field (such as context or description) on an audit log entry that permits mutation per policy, while immutable fields remain unchanged. This requires creating an audit log entry, then updating a permitted field and confirming audit trail correctness and restrictions.

dependencies.purpose: Create an audit log entry in advance so its auditLogId can be referenced and updated.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to update an immutable field on an audit log entry, such as the actor or action_type. The system should reject unauthorized or invalid modifications.

dependencies.purpose: Create a valid audit log entry for update attempt on immutable property.

scenarios.draft: Test the ability of an authorized admin to permanently remove an audit log by ID. Create an audit log entry, perform the delete, and verify that subsequent fetch attempts for that log fail (e.g., 404 not found). Attempting to access the deleted log should return a proper error message.

dependencies.purpose: Create an audit log entry first to ensure there is a record available for deletion.

scenarios.draft: Ensure that attempts by users without admin privileges to invoke the audit log deletion endpoint are denied, covering RBAC policy and audit compliance requirements.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure there is an audit log entry to test deletion attempt by a non-admin actor, which should be forbidden.

scenarios.draft: Test that an authenticated admin can retrieve a paginated list of notifications addressed to them from the notifications table. Ensure that only notifications scoped to the current admin are returned. Validate pagination and expected structure of the response, including references to related posts, comments, and actions as appropriate.

dependencies.purpose: Create at least one notification addressed to the admin to ensure there is a record to retrieve in the admin inbox.

scenarios.draft: Test that when an admin with no notifications invokes the endpoint, an empty list or appropriate response is returned without error.

Test that an authenticated moderator can access a list of their own notifications and that notifications intended for other roles or users are not included in the result set. Ensure correct RBAC scoping.

dependencies.purpose: Create and assign a notification specifically to a moderator to ensure there are relevant records to retrieve.

scenarios.draft: Ensure that unauthenticated or unauthorized users cannot access the moderator notifications endpoint, and that appropriate permission errors are returned.

Test successful retrieval of a member's notification setting detail by notificationSettingId. The test should set up a member user and ensure they have a notification setting record associated with their user ID. The member then requests their notification setting by its unique notificationSettingId. Expect the API to return the detailed configuration for notification delivery, including in-app/email enablement and per-category toggles, with all accessible fields populated. This verifies correct access and data delivery for the requesting member.

dependencies.purpose: Create a valid notification setting record for the member and extract the notificationSettingId for this test. Ensures the queried notificationSettingId exists and is owned by the member.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieval failure when a member attempts to access another user's notification setting record. Register two separate members with unique notification settings. Attempt to retrieve the notificationSettingId belonging to the other member. The API should deny access and return a forbidden error, ensuring strict RBAC and privacy control.

dependencies.purpose: Create notification setting for member A to supply a valid notificationSettingId.
Create a separate notification setting for member B (the actor making the request).

scenarios.draft: Test successful retrieval of a guest's own notification setting detail by notificationSettingId. Simulate guest registration/session, then create a notification setting for the guest. Use the guest session to retrieve their notificationSettingId. Confirm the API returns correct notification preferences for the guest, including delivery methods. This ensures proper personalization and guest privacy.

dependencies.purpose: Create or simulate a new guest session to obtain a guest user context.
Create a notification setting associated with the current guest session and extract the notificationSettingId.

scenarios.draft: Test failure response when a guest attempts to get a notification setting by a non-existent notificationSettingId. Register a guest session, then perform a GET on a notificationSettingId that does not exist. Verify the API returns a not found error, ensuring correct error handling for invalid identifiers.

dependencies.purpose: Register or simulate guest session to ensure valid guest context.

scenarios.draft: Test the ability of an admin to create a notification setting for a member. An admin account is authenticated. The admin creates a new notification setting specifying member as the target recipient. Ensure the returned object reflects the created setting and all ownership, channel, and category preferences are correctly assigned to the intended member. This test confirms admin privilege boundaries and creation business logic.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate an admin user for privileged access.
Register a member user so that the notification setting can target a specific member's userId.

scenarios.draft: Test error handling when an admin attempts to create a duplicate notification setting for the same user. An admin account creates notification settings for a target user (e.g., member). Then, the admin attempts to create another notification setting for the same member. The API should reject the second creation and return a duplication error, ensuring unique notification setting constraint per-user is enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate an admin user for privileged access.
Register a member for whom to create duplicate notification settings.
First, create a notification setting for this member to establish the initial record.

scenarios.draft: Test creation of notification settings by a moderator for themselves. Authenticate as a new moderator, then create a notification setting record linked to the moderator's own account. Verify that the setting is created and preferences are settable only for the current session user, ensuring correct self-service operation as a moderator.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin who will create a new moderator.
Register and authenticate a new moderator for test execution.

scenarios.draft: Test that a member can create a notification setting for their own account. A member is registered and authenticated; they create a notification setting via POST. Expect the API to persist and return the object with correct recipient ownership and notification preferences. This validates self-service notification customization for regular users.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate a member user who will create their own notification setting.

scenarios.draft: Test that members cannot create multiple notification settings for themselves. After successfully creating the first notification setting, attempt to create another for the same member account. The API should return a duplication error and prevent the second record, ensuring per-user uniqueness rule is properly enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate a member user.
Create the initial notification setting for this member.

scenarios.draft: Test successful update of an existing category-tag assignment by an admin. The scenario begins by creating a valid category and a tag as prerequisites, followed by creating an assignment linking a category to a tag. The test then updates this assignment to link the category to a different tag and checks if the update reflects correctly in the returned assignment record. This scenario verifies permission enforcement, schema compliance, and audit logging for the update operation.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new discussion board category as only admins can initiate category-tag assignments.
Create initial tag to be assigned to the category.
Create a second tag for reassignment test.
Assign the first tag to the category to set up data for the update test.

scenarios.draft: Test that attempting to update a category-tag assignment results in a validation error if the new category/tag pair already has an assignment (duplicates are not allowed). Steps: create two categories and two tags, assign both pairs, then attempt to update one assignment, changing its tag to a pair that already exists. Expect a conflict or validation error. This scenario checks business rule enforcement for uniqueness constraints at the junction table level.

dependencies.purpose: Create two categories for testing dual assignments.
Create two tags for testing dual assignments.
Assign first category-tag pair.
Assign second category-tag pair for uniqueness conflict setup.

scenarios.draft: Test that a moderator can update an existing category-tag assignment. After setting up by having an admin create a category and multiple tags, and assigning a tag to the category, a moderator updates the assignment to use a different tag. The scenario validates if the moderator has sufficient permissions, and the response includes the new assignment. It also covers audit trail aspects and permission boundaries.

dependencies.purpose: Admin creates category, as only admins can do so.
Admin creates tags for use in assignment and update.
Assign the initial tag to the category, establishing the record to be updated.

scenarios.draft: Test the successful deletion (hard delete) of an existing category-tag assignment by an admin. The process starts with creating a category and a tag, assigning the tag to the category, and then deleting the assignment using its unique ID. The test checks that the deleted record cannot be retrieved subsequently and that deletion is properly logged. This validates hard delete, permission checks, and compliance with immediate removal requirements.

dependencies.purpose: Create a category, prerequisite for tag assignment.
Create a tag for assignment.
Assign tag to category to enable a valid delete operation.

scenarios.draft: Test that attempting to delete a non-existent category-tag assignment (invalid or already deleted ID) returns an appropriate not found error. This scenario ensures business rules and error handling are enforced upon invalid delete attempts. No setup for assignment creation is needed; a random UUID or previously deleted ID can be used.

Test that a moderator can successfully delete (hard delete) a category-tag assignment. Steps: ensure setup by an admin (category and tag creations, assignment), then have a moderator issue the delete command. Test for correct deletion result, audit logging, and that the record is removed from listings.

dependencies.purpose: Admin creates a category for use in assignment.
Admin creates a tag to assign to the category.
Create the assignment for later deletion by a moderator.

scenarios.draft: Test that a guest (unauthenticated user) can retrieve the board's settings (such as title, description, logo URI, status) for display. This scenario does not require authentication or prior setup, and validates public information exposure and system branding logic.

Test that the settings returned reflect the latest updates made by an admin. The test first sets the board's settings via the admin update endpoint, then fetches them and checks whether the information matches the last update. This ensures proper consistency and update propagation for frontend display.

dependencies.purpose: Admin updates the board settings to a known new value for verification of freshness on fetch.

scenarios.draft: Test searching and paginating authentication tokens with a combination of valid filters such as actor_type, issued_at date range, and revoked status. The test should confirm that only tokens matching the search/filter criteria are returned and that pagination metadata is accurate. Precondition: ensure there exist tokens for multiple actor types (admin, member, moderator, guest) and different revoked statuses.

dependencies.purpose: Create several authentication tokens for different actor types and states to populate the dataset for search/filter scenarios.

scenarios.draft: Test error handling when invalid or incorrectly formatted search/filter criteria are provided (e.g., malformed UUID, unsupported actor_type value). The API should return a meaningful validation error and must not expose sensitive operational details.

Test the ability to retrieve authentication tokens in multiple pages, ensuring sorting works as requested (e.g., by issued_at descending or ascending). The test should verify that results are consistent over navigated pages and sorting order.

dependencies.purpose: Create enough authentication tokens to require at least two pages of data when using default or minimal page sizes.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving the details of a specific authentication token by a valid UUID. The response should include all non-sensitive fields for the token and match data previously created. Precondition: create at least one valid authentication token and use its generated ID in the test.

dependencies.purpose: Create a valid authentication token and use its ID for retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test requesting authentication token details using an invalid or non-existent UUID. The test should verify that a 404 Not Found or appropriate error is returned and that no sensitive information is leaked in the error message.

Test successful creation of an authentication token using valid actor_type and actor_id. The resulting response should include all expected fields (omitting the raw token string if policy requires). Precondition: there must be a valid actor (e.g., admin, member, moderator, or guest) to assign as the token's owner.

Test attempt to create an authentication token with a token value that already exists (if uniqueness is enforced on the token string). Expect the API to reject the request and return an error indicating duplicate token violation.

dependencies.purpose: Create an initial authentication token with a specific token value to ensure the subsequent duplicate attempt triggers a conflict.

scenarios.draft: Test creation attempt using a non-existent or invalid actor_id (e.g., non-UUID format or referencing a deleted user). The API should return a validation or not-found error and no token is created.

Test successfully revoking an authentication token by updating the revoked status. The response should show the token as revoked and unexpired (if not expired already). Precondition: a valid non-revoked token must exist to be updated.

dependencies.purpose: Create a valid, non-revoked authentication token to be updated during the test.

scenarios.draft: Test updating a non-existent or invalid authentication token ID. The API should return a 404 or appropriate error indicating the target was not found and no update occurs.
Test updating a token with invalid or empty fields (e.g., expiration in the past, revoked with invalid value, etc.). The API should reject the update and return detailed validation errors.

dependencies.purpose: Create an authentication token to attempt an invalid update scenario (such as setting an already-expired date).

scenarios.draft: Test successfully deleting an authentication token by its valid ID. After deletion, the token should no longer be retrievable via GET, and the operation should be irrevocable. Precondition: create a valid authentication token for deletion.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new authentication token whose ID will be used for the deletion test.

scenarios.draft: Test attempting to delete a token with an invalid or non-existent UUID. Expect a meaningful error code (typically 404 Not Found) with no side effects or sensitive data exposure.

Test successful retrieval of all notification settings for an authenticated admin user. The test should verify that only the admin's own notification settings are returned, with delivery and category preferences present for each record. Pagination should be validated for larger result sets. All returned records must be properly scoped to the admin's user ID, and access should be denied for non-privileged users (covered in separate scenario).

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin account for authentication and authorization context.

scenarios.draft: Verify that an admin cannot retrieve notification settings for other users by attempting the endpoint as a different admin, moderator, member, or guest. Only the authenticated user's own notification settings should be accessible. An attempt to access another user’s settings should be forbidden or return an empty result set, as appropriate.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin account for authentication and authorization context.
Create a moderator account for testing cross-role access restrictions.
Create a member account for testing access restrictions.

scenarios.draft: Test that a moderator can retrieve all their own notification settings, with each entry containing proper delivery and category preferences. The test should cover the correct scoping of results to the authenticated moderator and validation of pagination. Attempting to access settings for any other user must not be allowed or must return no results (privacy enforcement).

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderator account for authentication and authorization context.

scenarios.draft: Test that non-moderator users (members, guests) cannot access notification settings through the moderator endpoint. Attempting to access this endpoint as a non-moderator should result in access forbidden or an authentication error, ensuring enforcement of role-based access control.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account (non-moderator) for negative access test.

scenarios.draft: Test that a member can retrieve all of their own notification settings, ensuring that delivery and category preferences are returned as per the schema. The test must validate that only the current member’s settings are shown and that pagination metadata is accurate when result sets are large.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account to prepare the user context for notification settings retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test the scenario where a member account is deactivated or not active. The member should not be able to retrieve notification settings after deactivation, and the API should return an authentication or access error as per business logic.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account.
Deactivate or set the 'is_active' flag to false for the test member account.

scenarios.draft: Test that a guest (unauthenticated, session-based user) can access their own notification settings when a valid guest session is established. The test should verify that only the current guest’s notification settings are returned and that settings are properly initialized during guest onboarding. Edge cases include expired sessions or no settings configured, in which case the result should be empty or a valid notification settings structure with default values.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new guest session by registering a guest access record for the test context.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can filter their notification settings by specific categories (e.g., moderation, reply, vote) using the search endpoint. The test should check for accurate filtering and pagination. The request should include diverse setting entries for the admin and attempt a filtered search, verifying that only matching records are returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin account to configure multiple notification settings of different categories for search testing.
Create several notification settings entries with varying categories for the admin account.

scenarios.draft: Test for correct error handling when the admin sends an invalid filter or search query (such as non-existent category values, malformed request body, or date parameters in the wrong format). The API should return relevant validation errors, not internal errors or unhelpful failure codes.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin account to submit search requests with intentionally invalid or malformed parameters.

scenarios.draft: Test that a moderator can search and filter their notification settings using various advanced parameters such as delivery channel (in-app/email), category toggles (like moderation, reply, vote), and time ranges. Ensure search returns only the notification settings relevant to the authenticated moderator. Validate that pagination and sorting work as expected. Prepare by creating/modifying a variety of notification settings for the moderator via the relevant creation endpoint.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple notification settings records for the moderator, each with different delivery channels and categories to enable realistic search coverage.

scenarios.draft: Verify that access to search notification settings with advanced parameters is denied if the user is not authenticated as a moderator or above. Try searching as a guest or member and expect a permission error, confirming role-based access is enforced for this moderator endpoint.

Verify that a member can search and filter their own notification settings using advanced parameters such as delivery channel, category toggles, and time ranges. Results should only include this member's records and be properly paginated/sorted. Pre-create multiple settings via the member notification settings creation endpoint for test coverage.

dependencies.purpose: Create several notification settings for the same member with different filter combinations to verify search responses include all and only their own records.

scenarios.draft: Check that an unauthenticated or unauthorized request to this endpoint is denied with an appropriate error. Attempt to use the endpoint as a guest or a different member and ensure permission rules are correctly enforced so members can't search other users' notification settings.

Confirm a guest may search and filter their notification settings using allowed parameters such as delivery type, notification category, or time range. The results must only reflect the settings for the authenticated guest session. Ensure advanced queries cannot return or access other guests’ or members’ settings. Precondition: Register a guest notification setting and additional guest sessions if needed for testing cross-session security.

dependencies.purpose: Create one or more notification settings for the active guest session and optionally others to test isolation between sessions.

scenarios.draft: Test that a guest attempting to search notification settings of a different guest session or of a member, moderator, or admin receives access denied or empty results, ensuring privacy and RBAC are enforced in the endpoint.

Test that an admin can retrieve the full details of a notification settings record they own by providing the notificationSettingId. Verify correct details are returned for the authenticated admin and that all preference fields (delivery channels, per-category toggles) are reflected accurately. Create such a settings record for the admin beforehand and use its ID for the GET request.

dependencies.purpose: Create a notification settings record for the admin user so that its ID can be used for the GET detail test.

scenarios.draft: Ensure that if an admin user attempts to retrieve a notification settings record not owned by them (for example, a member's or different admin's settings), the endpoint returns a forbidden or not found error, upholding privacy and data access controls. Attempt GET with the ID of a notification setting belonging to another user type or admin and check the error response.

dependencies.purpose: Create a notification settings record for a member; use its ID to simulate cross-user/admin unauthorized GET attempts.

scenarios.draft: Test that a moderator can retrieve their own notification settings using the notificationSettingId, verifying the response contains all preference fields and delivery configurations as expected. A pre-existing settings record for the moderator is needed; create one before running the GET call.

dependencies.purpose: Create a notification settings record for the moderator so that it can be fetched by get detail.

scenarios.draft: Test that a moderator cannot access the detail of another user's notification setting, such as a member’s or another moderator’s. Attempt to GET a notificationSettingId belonging to a different user and verify the endpoint denies this access with the correct error or null result.

dependencies.purpose: Create a notification setting for a member to use its ID for unauthorized access attempt by the moderator.

scenarios.draft: Test admin notification creation with fully valid input. Log in as an admin. Submit a creation request with all required fields, including a valid recipient (e.g., a member's ID or an admin's own ID), a notification message, correct category/type, and correct references. Verify that the notification is not only created but also linked to the appropriate recipient and visible in their notification inbox. Expected: 201 Created, notification appears for the intended recipient.

Test failure to create notification when required fields are missing. Log in as an admin. Attempt to create a notification while omitting mandatory fields (e.g., message, recipient ID, or category). The API should reject the request and return validation errors indicating which fields are missing. Expected: 400 Bad Request with error details.

Validate business error handling for notification creation when the recipient (admin_id, moderator_id, member_id, or guest_id) does not exist or is deactivated. Log in as admin, try to create a notification for a nonexistent or deactivated recipient. The API should respond with an error indicating recipient not found or not active. Expected: 404 Not Found or 422 Unprocessable Entity with error reason.

Test logic that prevents duplicate notifications for the same event to the same recipient if business logic requires deduplication. Simulate creating a notification for a recipient for a specific event, then attempt to create the exact notification again. If deduplication or idempotency is enforced, the system should block the duplicate or return relevant status. Expected: Either an error or status indicating duplication logic as implemented.

Test successful notification creation by a moderator for a valid recipient (admin, moderator, member, or guest). Verify that all mandatory fields are present and the new notification is visible to the intended recipient. Expected: 201 Created, notification delivered and shown in recipient's notification list.

Attempt to create a notification as moderator while omitting one or more required fields (such as recipient or message). API should reject the request and provide a clear validation error. Expected: 400 Bad Request with error message indicating missing fields.

Try to send a notification to a non-existent or inactive recipient (admin, moderator, member, or guest). The system should reject the request, indicating the recipient does not exist or is inactive. Expected: 404 Not Found or 422 Unprocessable Entity with clear explanation.

Test marking a notification as read via update by the admin. Authenticate as the admin. Update a notification (using a valid notificationId owned by the admin) to set its 'is_read' field to true. Confirm that the notification's state is updated only for the correct admin and that the change is persisted. Expected: 200 OK, notification is marked as read in the admin's list.

dependencies.purpose: First, create a notification to get a valid notificationId for update.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to update a notification with a non-existent or unauthorized notificationId as admin. The API should return an error indicating the notification was not found or access is forbidden. Expected: 404 Not Found or 403 Forbidden.

Attempt to update immutable or restricted fields in a notification (e.g., attempt to change recipient or non-updatable metadata). The API should reject such updates to ensure business rules and data integrity. Expected: 400 Bad Request or 422 Unprocessable Entity with appropriate error details.

dependencies.purpose: Create a notification first so there is a target notification to update.

scenarios.draft: Test moderator marking their own notification as read. As an authenticated moderator, update an owned notification using its notificationId to set 'is_read' to true. Confirm that the updated status is only reflected for this moderator's view. Expected: 200 OK and notification is now "read".

dependencies.purpose: Create a notification for the moderator to generate a valid notificationId.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to update a notification as moderator, referencing an invalid or non-existent notificationId. Expected: 404 Not Found or 403 Forbidden as appropriate, verifying secure resource access.

Attempt to update a notification not intended for the current moderator, testing access control logic. The API should reject access or silently disallow update so that only the rightful recipient or privileged actor can change notification state. Expected: 403 Forbidden or similar.

dependencies.purpose: Create a notification for a different admin or recipient to test access control.

scenarios.draft: Test member updating their own notification to mark it as read. As a logged-in member, update notificationId with 'is_read: true'. Confirm the change is accepted and only affects that member's inbox. Expected: 200 OK, notification marked as read.

dependencies.purpose: Admin creates a notification for the member account to set up a valid notificationId for the member to update.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to update a notification using a notificationId that does not exist, as a member. The response should be a 404 Not Found, and no notification is updated.

Attempt by a member to update a notification addressed to a different user (admin, moderator, or another member). This should be rejected to enforce RBAC and data privacy. Expected: 403 Forbidden or 404 Not Found.

dependencies.purpose: Create a notification for another user (different member or moderator) to test access restriction.

scenarios.draft: As a moderator, search for comments using common filtering criteria such as keywords in the body, member ID, post ID, and date ranges. Confirm results paginate correctly and reflect only permitted comment visibility according to moderator role (including soft-deleted if policy allows).

dependencies.purpose: Create sample comments with diverse bodies, members, posts, and timestamps to populate data for search and filtering tests.

scenarios.draft: Use advanced search filters to retrieve only comments under a specific parent comment, verifying threaded conversations' correct hierarchical retrieval in the backend for moderation review. Paged results must match thread depth and filter constraints set in the request.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple comments with explicit parent-child relationships to form threaded comment trees for search testing.

scenarios.draft: Verify that, as a moderator, soft-deleted comments (comments with deleted_at set) are returned when searching with appropriate filters. Ensure that RBAC correctly exposes these to moderators but not to ordinary members. Confirm that deleted comments are labeled appropriately in the response.

dependencies.purpose: Create comments, then soft-delete selected ones to create a test set that includes both active and deleted comments.
Soft-delete specific comments as setup, using their IDs from previous creations for later search verification.

scenarios.draft: Attempt a comment search as moderator with invalid filter criteria, such as an improperly formatted date, excessively large page size, or a non-existent member ID. Confirm the system returns a clear validation error and does not process the query.

As an admin, perform an advanced search over comments using multiple filters jointly (body content, author member ID, post ID, date ranges, and parent ID). Validate that paginated results match all search parameters and show both regular and soft-deleted comments according to RBAC.

dependencies.purpose: Create a collection of comments with varied content, parent-child structure, authors, and posts to facilitate comprehensive search scenarios.

scenarios.draft: Conduct a search as admin with filter criteria guaranteed not to match any existing comments (e.g., nonsensical body text, non-existent member ID). Ensure that an empty result set and correct pagination metadata are returned.

Attempt to search comments with a page size exceeding the maximum allowed by system configuration. Verify that the API correctly returns an error indicating invalid page size, enforcing pagination limits.

A logged-in member retrieves the full details of a comment they authored. Confirm all fields—including content, author info, post linkage, parent-child references, timestamps, and absence of deleted_at for active comments—are correctly returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new comment authored by the member to ensure its existence for retrieval.

scenarios.draft: A member retrieves a comment made by another member on a public post. Confirm that the full details are returned, provided the requesting user has permission to view the post and comment.

dependencies.purpose: Create a public post authored by one member.
Create a comment on the public post by a different member.

scenarios.draft: A member attempts to fetch details of a comment on a post they do not have access to (e.g., private post) or one that has been soft-deleted. The system should return a forbidden/not found error and not leak data about the restricted or deleted comment.

dependencies.purpose: Create a private post or a post the member cannot access.
Create a comment under the private post.
Soft-delete another comment for the same scenario group.

scenarios.draft: A moderator retrieves the full details of a comment, including comments that have been soft-deleted (deleted_at set). Confirm that all fields, including deletion info, are populated for moderator audit and review.

dependencies.purpose: Create one or more comments.
Soft-delete a target comment to verify retrieval of deleted status by moderator.

scenarios.draft: As a moderator, fetch the details of a comment that resides in a post or thread restricted from regular member access (e.g., in a private or moderated section). Confirm that moderators are granted access and all comment detail fields are present.

dependencies.purpose: Create a private/moderated post with restricted access.
Add a comment to the restricted post.

scenarios.draft: Admin retrieves the full details of any comment, including those soft-deleted or on private posts. Confirm the API returns all atomic schema fields, deleted_at (if any), and relationships for legal or compliance audits.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment as a regular member.
Soft-delete that comment to test admin retrieval.

scenarios.draft: As admin, attempt to retrieve a comment with a non-existing or improperly formatted UUID. Confirm the API returns a not found or validation error, never leaking comment existence details for security compliance.

Test retrieving the detailed profile of a specific member as a moderator when the member exists. First, create a member account to ensure there is a valid memberId. Then, as an authenticated moderator, attempt to fetch the details of that member. The expected outcome is that the full profile, including administrative and audit fields, is returned with no sensitive information (like password hash), and the operation succeeds for authorized roles.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member so as to have a valid memberId to query for.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving member details as a moderator when the specified memberId does not exist. As an authenticated moderator, attempt to fetch details for a non-existent or randomly generated member UUID. The expected outcome is that the endpoint returns an appropriate 404 error or not found response, verifying error handling for invalid member references.

Test attempting to retrieve member details as a non-privileged user or using an invalid/expired session. Attempt to fetch details as a user without moderator/admin privileges or with no authentication. The expected outcome is an authentication or authorization error, verifying strict RBAC enforcement.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member, if needed, to avoid false negatives on nonexistence errors.

scenarios.draft: Test successful registration of a new member using valid display name, email, and a strong password that meets business policy. Submit the registration request as a guest (unauthenticated). Expected outcome is a successful creation response containing the new member's full profile, proper initialization of verification and status fields, and audit timestamps.

Test member registration failure due to using an email address that already exists in the system. First, create an initial member with a specific unique email. Then, attempt to register another member using the same email. The expected outcome is a validation error indicating email uniqueness violation and failure to create the account.

dependencies.purpose: Create the first member with the given email to enforce uniqueness check for the second registration.

scenarios.draft: Test failure when registering a new member with an invalid email format in the registration payload. Submit a request with an email not conforming to standard email format. Expected outcome is a validation error indicating improper formatting and no member account created.

Test failure when attempting to create a new member with a weak password that does not meet system strength requirements. Submit the registration with a too-short or commonly used password. Expect validation error, with details specifying the password policy violation, and no account is created.

Test successful updating of a member's profile by an admin. First, create a member, then as an admin, update editable fields such as display name or verification status. The expected outcome is that the member's profile is updated, audit logs are adjusted, and all changes are reflected in the response. Only permitted fields should be updatable, and business logic such as email uniqueness must be enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new member to use in update scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test failure when an admin tries updating a member's email address to one already in use by another member. First, create two members with unique emails. As an admin, attempt to update the second member's email to match the first. The expected outcome is a validation error specifying the uniqueness violation.

dependencies.purpose: Create the first member with a unique email.
Create the second member whose email will be updated to a duplicate.

scenarios.draft: Test updating a member profile with invalid data (e.g., invalid email format, weak password, or restricted field modifications) as an admin. The expected result is a detailed error message for the specific violation (invalid email format, weak password, or unmodifiable field), and the original member information remains unchanged.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member for testing invalid update scenarios.

scenarios.draft: Test that a logged-in member can successfully update their own profile fields, such as display name or password, following proper authentication. Create a member account, log in as that member, and submit a valid update. The expected outcome is a successful profile update and confirmation in the response.

dependencies.purpose: Create the member who will perform self-update.

scenarios.draft: Test that a member attempting to update their email to an invalid format receives a validation error and that the profile is not updated. Validate that detailed feedback is given and audit logs reflect the attempted change.

dependencies.purpose: Create the member for the scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test a member attempting to update another member's profile (not their own), which should fail due to insufficient permissions. Validate that the system enforces ownership and returns an authorization error, leaving data unchanged.

dependencies.purpose: Create at least two member accounts: one as the actor and one as the target of the update.

scenarios.draft: Test successful permanent deletion of a member by an admin. First, create a new member, then as an admin, perform the delete operation using the member's ID. Confirm the member is no longer retrievable and all associations are properly handled or cascaded as per business logic.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new member to be deleted.

scenarios.draft: Test deletion of a non-existent member by an admin. Attempt to delete a memberId that does not exist. The expected result is an appropriate not found error (404) or business rule violation message, and data integrity is maintained.

Test attempting to delete a member without admin privileges or using an invalid/expired token. Attempt the deletion as a non-admin account or unauthenticated session. The expected result is an authorization error and no member data is deleted.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member to use as the target for unauthorized deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test the ability for a guest user to mark a notification as read through this endpoint. Begin by ensuring a guest session exists and at least one notification, addressed to this session, has been delivered (using notification creation endpoints or guest actions that would trigger notifications). Attempt to update the notification with the is_read property set to true, and verify the read status is updated. Ensure that the guest session has the correct notificationId and proper authentication token/session if required.

dependencies.purpose: Register a guest session to obtain a guestId required for notification assignment and identification.
Create and deliver a notification to the guest user so there is a real notificationId to update.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to update a notification as a guest for which the current session is NOT the recipient. This should return a forbidden or unauthorized error, ensuring guests can only alter their own notifications. Set up by creating a guest and issuing notifications to multiple guestIds, then have one guest attempt to update another's notificationId.

dependencies.purpose: Register two separate guest sessions (A and B), both with their own guestIds, to create isolation of guest resources.
Create notifications, assigning one to guest A and another to guest B, to be able to test cross-guest update attempt.

scenarios.draft: Verify that an admin user can successfully delete their own notification by notificationId. First, ensure an admin account exists and a notification is issued to this admin (either by system action or via notification creation endpoint). Then invoke the delete operation and confirm that the notification is removed and no longer accessible to the admin, checking that all schema-side references are properly cleaned up.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin account to act as the recipient of the notification.
Deliver a notification specifically addressed to the new admin and retrieve the notificationId for deletion.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to delete a notification as an admin, where the notification belongs to another user (e.g., another admin, moderator, member, or guest). The operation should be forbidden and must return a proper error code/status. The test should create notifications for multiple users and attempt cross-user deletion to ensure RBAC integrity.

dependencies.purpose: Create two admin accounts, each able to independently receive notifications.
Issue separate notifications to each admin (or other users/roles, such as moderators/members/guests).

scenarios.draft: Test that a moderator can successfully delete their own notification. Create a moderator account, send a notification to this moderator, and then delete it, verifying its removal from the system and confirming its inaccessibility after deletion.

dependencies.purpose: Register a moderator who will be the notification recipient.
Send a notification to the newly created moderator to set up test deletion.

scenarios.draft: Ensure that a moderator cannot delete a notification that belongs to a different user (another moderator, admin, member, or guest). Attempting this should result in a forbidden or unauthorized error. Set up two users (moderators or other roles), issue notifications to each, and attempt a cross-user deletion.

dependencies.purpose: Register two moderator accounts for independent notification assignment.
Send notifications targeted to each moderator (or other roles for wider cross-role testing).

scenarios.draft: Verify that a member can delete notifications addressed to them. Register a member, send a notification to this member, perform the delete operation, and confirm the notification is no longer accessible.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new member who will receive test notifications.
Create and deliver a notification to the member, acquiring the notificationId for deletion.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to delete a notification as a member where the notificationId is assigned to a different member. This should return a forbidden/unauthorized error and leave the other member's notification untouched. Register two members, assign notifications, and perform a cross-user deletion attempt.

dependencies.purpose: Create two members for isolated resource ownership (member A and member B).
Deliver notifications to both members, allowing for attempted cross-member deletion.

scenarios.draft: Confirm that a guest user can delete their own notification. First, create a guest session and assign a notification to that guest. Perform the delete and verify that the notification is permanently removed, validating guest-specific RBAC policies.

dependencies.purpose: Initiate a guest session and get a guestId for notification addressing.
Issue a notification to the guest session, obtaining its notificationId for subsequent deletion.

scenarios.draft: Check that a guest cannot delete another guest's notification. With two guest sessions created, each with notifications, have one guest attempt to delete a notification belonging to the other. The system should reject the action with a forbidden or unauthorized error, maintaining data privacy and role isolation.

dependencies.purpose: Create two distinct guest sessions with unique guestIds.
Send notifications to each guest separately, so that guest A can attempt to delete guest B's notification (and expect an error).

scenarios.draft: Test the ability of a moderator to delete a specific post vote by its ID. First, create a member, a moderator, and a post as the member. Then, cast a vote on the post as the member. Finally, as the moderator, delete the vote using this endpoint and verify that the vote is removed from the database. Ensure audit logs reflect the deletion action.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post as a member so there is a post to vote on.
Cast a vote on the post as the member to generate a post vote that can be deleted.

scenarios.draft: Test error handling when an attempt is made to delete a post vote with a non-existent or invalid postVoteId. As a moderator, use a valid postId but an invalid or random UUID for postVoteId, and verify that the system returns a not found error and logs the attempt for audit purposes.

Test that non-moderators (such as a member) cannot delete a post vote using the moderator endpoint. After creating a post and a vote as a member, have the member attempt to delete the vote via this endpoint, and verify that an authorization error is returned and no deletion occurs.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post as a member so there is a post to vote on.
Cast a vote on the post as the member to generate a post vote that an unauthorized user will attempt to delete.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can successfully delete a post vote. Create a member, admin, and post as the member. The member votes on the post. The admin then deletes the vote by this endpoint and validation checks that the vote is removed, and audit logs reflect the admin action.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post as a member for voting.
Cast the vote as the member to produce a deletable vote.

scenarios.draft: Test the case when the admin attempts to delete a non-existent post vote. Supply a valid postId and a random UUID as postVoteId. The system must respond with a not found error and record the attempt in the audit trail.

Ensure RBAC prevents non-admin roles from deleting a post vote via the admin endpoint. After a member creates and votes on a post, attempt to delete the vote as a member or unauthorized role, and check for proper permission denial and retention of the vote.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post for the vote.
Record a member's vote to attempt unauthorized deletion by a non-admin.

scenarios.draft: Test that an authenticated member can successfully retrieve the list of all votes for a specific comment. First, create a post and a comment on that post, then cast multiple votes (upvote and downvote) on the comment by various members. Use this endpoint as one of the voting members to fetch all votes for the comment and verify correct pagination and vote record structure, including upvote/downvote and voter data.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post to host the comment.
Create a comment on the post to be voted on.
Submit at least one upvote and one downvote from different members for the comment.

scenarios.draft: Test behavior when trying to list votes for a commentId that does not exist. Attempt to fetch votes for a random UUID and verify that the API returns a not found error, with no data leakage.

Verify that an unauthenticated or unauthorized user (guest) is prevented from accessing the comment votes endpoint. Attempt to access this endpoint without authentication, expecting permission denied or 401/403 response code.

Test advanced search for comment votes using type and date range filters. After creating a post and comment, multiple members vote (both upvote and downvote) at different times. Use this endpoint with filters to fetch only upvotes or only downvotes, or votes cast within a certain time period, and check that results match the criteria.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post to allow comment creation.
Add a comment for voting.
Record votes from multiple members on the target comment at distinct times.

scenarios.draft: Test the reaction of the endpoint to invalid search/filter criteria (e.g., invalid vote type, malformed parameters, or out-of-bounds dates). Ensure the API returns a validation error and does not expose internal data.

Ensure that an unauthorized or unauthenticated user cannot perform advanced searches for comment votes. Attempt to use this endpoint as a guest or without credentials and verify the rejection and no data exposure.

Verify a member can retrieve details of a specific comment vote by its ID. After creating a comment and voting as a member, use this endpoint to fetch the vote details and validate all relevant fields are returned (voter, type, timestamps).

dependencies.purpose: Create a post for the comment.
Create a comment to be voted on.
Cast a vote as the member and capture the vote ID for retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test the endpoint's response when requesting comment vote details for a non-existent or malformed commentVoteId. Ensure the system returns not found error and no sensitive info.

Test that guests and unauthorized users cannot retrieve details of a specific comment vote. Attempt to use this endpoint without valid member authentication, verifying permission denial with no data breach.

Verify that an admin can permanently delete a guest session record by supplying a valid guestId. Start by registering a new guest session so the ID is known, then perform the DELETE operation and confirm the session is removed from the database and cannot be retrieved afterwards. Also, validate that audit logs (if implemented elsewhere) reflect this action.

dependencies.purpose: To create a new guest session and obtain a guestId for deletion testing.

scenarios.draft: Test that attempting to delete a guest session with a non-existent or already-deleted guestId results in a proper error response, such as 404 not found. Ensure no side effects are caused by this invalid deletion attempt.

Ensure that only users with admin privileges can perform guest record deletions. Attempt to delete a guest session as a non-admin (or unauthenticated) user and confirm access is denied with an appropriate error response (e.g., 403 Forbidden).

dependencies.purpose: To create a guest session and guarantee its presence for attempted unauthorized deletion.

scenarios.draft: Validate that both guests and authenticated members can retrieve a paginated list of discussion board posts. Ensure only non-deleted posts are returned, and that the list adheres to privacy and category visibility (public/private) rules. Test both guest and member access to determine RBAC correctly affects results.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new member to test authenticated member access.

scenarios.draft: Test the scenario in which there are no posts in the system or all posts are soft-deleted. Confirm that the response is an empty result set and that pagination metadata accurately reflects zero results.
Create posts and then soft-delete some of them. Verify the API does not include soft-deleted posts in the response while active posts remain visible. Validate for both guests and members.

dependencies.purpose: Create posts for testing (requires member creation).
Soft-delete published posts to confirm exclusion from listings.

scenarios.draft: Verify that the advanced post search allows filtering posts by category, tag, and author. Create sample posts with different categories, tags, and authors, then perform a filtered search to confirm only matching posts are returned. Also ensure pagination and sorting options work as specified.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple posts with various categories, tags, and authors for search filtering.

scenarios.draft: Ensure that posts which are soft-deleted do not appear in advanced search results. Create and soft-delete a post, then attempt to search for it with criteria that would normally match. Confirm the result does not include the soft-deleted post.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post for testing.
Soft-delete the post to set up exclusion from search.

scenarios.draft: Submit a search request with malformed or logically invalid parameters (e.g., invalid UUIDs, unsupported filters, or out-of-bounds pagination). Verify the API returns validation errors and does not process the query.

Confirm that fetching post details with a valid, public postId returns all expected data, including author, categories, and tags. Ensure this works for both guests and members, and that only appropriate metadata is exposed per RBAC.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new post to get a valid postId for detail fetch.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to retrieve post details using a non-existent or incorrectly-formatted postId. Verify that the API responds with an appropriate error such as 404 not found or validation error.

Test that attempting to fetch details for a post that has been soft-deleted does not return the post for normal users (guests, members), but may be retrievable by admins or moderators if permitted by policy.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post for testing.
Soft-delete the post to test restricted visibility in detail view.

scenarios.draft: Verify that a member can successfully create a post by providing only the mandatory fields: author memberId, title, and body (with optional parent_id omitted). Confirm the post is created with correct metadata and appears in listings.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new member to create and own the post.

scenarios.draft: Test that a member can create a new post and assign categories and tags if those fields are supported in the create schema. Ensure assignments are reflected in the response and listings, and related dependencies (categories, tags) must exist before assignment.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member to create the post.
Fetch available categories to assign to the post.
Fetch available tags to assign to the post.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to create a post as an unauthenticated user (or with improper credentials). Confirm the API responds with an authorization or authentication error, preventing post creation.

Attempt to create a post with invalid data such as missing required fields, invalid memberId, or violating title/body constraints (e.g., excessively long strings, empty fields). Confirm validation errors are returned and no post is created.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member for use in testing invalid post creation scenarios.

scenarios.draft: Test successful creation of a new tag by an admin, providing a unique label, a description, and a color. Confirm the response includes all metadata, and the new tag is available for selection/assignment.

Test failure when attempting to create a tag with a label that already exists in the discussion board tags table. First create a tag with a given label, then attempt to create another with the same label, expecting a uniqueness constraint violation error and a clear error message.

dependencies.purpose: Create the initial tag with a specific label to set up a duplicate label scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test failure of tag creation when the required 'label' field is omitted from the request. Validation should fail, and the API must return an error indicating the missing required field.

Test successful retrieval of an existing tag's full details by its tagId. Ensure returned data matches the created tag's label, description, color, and metadata. The tag must already exist—set up by admin creation flow.

dependencies.purpose: Create a tag as setup, so its tagId can be used for retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieval of a tag by a tagId that does not exist in the system. The API should return an appropriate not found (404) error response.

Test that a guest attempting to fetch a soft-deleted tag by tagId does not receive the tag details or receives a forbidden/not found error. The tag should be created, soft-deleted by admin, and then retrieved as guest.

dependencies.purpose: Create a tag for test initialization.
Soft-delete the tag to simulate a deleted state.

scenarios.draft: Test that updating a tag's color with an improperly formatted value (e.g., invalid hex code) results in a validation error. This confirms proper input validation for color fields.

dependencies.purpose: Create a tag for update scenario.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to update a tag using a tagId that does not exist. Confirm that the API returns a 404 not found error response.

Execute the first soft-delete operation.

Create at least one category for assignment.
Assign the tag to the category to establish a category-tag assignment for the test.

Test that unauthenticated requests to retrieve all category-tag assignments are denied or do not return sensitive configuration data, verifying that proper authorization is enforced.

The API should validate all references, store the report, and return the created report marked as pending or under_review. dependencies.purpose: Register a new member account to use as the reporting user.
