Ensure the returned object reflects the created setting and all ownership, channel, and category preferences are correctly assigned to the intended member. This test confirms admin privilege boundaries and creation business logic.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate an admin user for privileged access.
Register a member user so that the notification setting can target a specific member's userId.

scenario.draft: Test error handling when an admin attempts to create a duplicate notification setting for the same user. An admin account creates notification settings for a target user (e.g., member). Then, the admin attempts to create another notification setting for the same member. The API should reject the second creation and return a duplication error, ensuring unique notification setting constraint per-user is enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate an admin user for privileged access.
Register a member for whom to create duplicate notification settings.
First, create a notification setting for this member to establish the initial record.

scenario.draft: Test creation of notification settings by a moderator for themselves. Authenticate as a new moderator, then create a notification setting record linked to the moderator's own account. Verify that the setting is created and preferences are settable only for the current session user, ensuring correct self-service operation as a moderator.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin who will create a new moderator.
Register and authenticate a new moderator for test execution.

scenario.draft: Test that a member can create a notification setting for their own account. A member is registered and authenticated; they create a notification setting via POST. Expect the API to persist and return the object with correct recipient ownership and notification preferences. This validates self-service notification customization for regular users.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate a member user who will create their own notification setting.

scenario.draft: Test that members cannot create multiple notification settings for themselves. After successfully creating the first notification setting, attempt to create another for the same member account. The API should return a duplication error and prevent the second record, ensuring per-user uniqueness rule is properly enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate a member user.
Create the initial notification setting for this member.

scenario.draft: Test successful update of an existing category-tag assignment by an admin. The scenario begins by creating a valid category and a tag as prerequisites, followed by creating an assignment linking a category to a tag. The test then updates this assignment to link the category to a different tag and checks if the update reflects correctly in the returned assignment record. This scenario verifies permission enforcement, schema compliance, and audit logging for the update operation.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new discussion board category as only admins can initiate category-tag assignments.
Create initial tag to be assigned to the category.
Create a second tag for reassignment test.
Assign the first tag to the category to set up data for the update test.

scenario.draft: Test that attempting to update a category-tag assignment results in a validation error if the new category/tag pair already has an assignment (duplicates are not allowed). Steps: create two categories and two tags, assign both pairs, then attempt to update one assignment, changing its tag to a pair that already exists. Expect a conflict or validation error. This scenario checks business rule enforcement for uniqueness constraints at the junction table level.

dependencies.purpose: Create two categories for testing dual assignments.
Create two tags for testing dual assignments.
Assign first category-tag pair.
Assign second category-tag pair for uniqueness conflict setup.

scenario.draft: Test that a moderator can update an existing category-tag assignment. After setting up by having an admin create a category and multiple tags, and assigning a tag to the category, a moderator updates the assignment to use a different tag. The scenario validates if the moderator has sufficient permissions, and the response includes the new assignment. It also covers audit trail aspects and permission boundaries.

dependencies.purpose: Admin creates category, as only admins can do so.
Admin creates tags for use in assignment and update.
Assign the initial tag to the category, establishing the record to be updated.

scenario.draft: Test the successful deletion (hard delete) of an existing category-tag assignment by an admin. The process starts with creating a category and a tag, assigning the tag to the category, and then deleting the assignment using its unique ID. The test checks that the deleted record cannot be retrieved subsequently and that deletion is properly logged. This validates hard delete, permission checks, and compliance with immediate removal requirements.

dependencies.purpose: Create a category, prerequisite for tag assignment.
Create a tag for assignment.
Assign tag to category to enable a valid delete operation.

scenario.draft: Test that attempting to delete a non-existent category-tag assignment (invalid or already deleted ID) returns an appropriate not found error. This scenario ensures business rules and error handling are enforced upon invalid delete attempts. No setup for assignment creation is needed; a random UUID or previously deleted ID can be used.

Test that a moderator can successfully delete (hard delete) a category-tag assignment. Steps: ensure setup by an admin (category and tag creations, assignment), then have a moderator issue the delete command. Test for correct deletion result, audit logging, and that the record is removed from listings.

dependencies.purpose: Admin creates a category for use in assignment.
Admin creates a tag to assign to the category.
Create the assignment for later deletion by a moderator.

scenario.draft: Test that a guest (unauthenticated user) can retrieve the board's settings (such as title, description, logo URI, status) for display. This scenario does not require authentication or prior setup, and validates public information exposure and system branding logic.

Test that the settings returned reflect the latest updates made by an admin. The test first sets the board's settings via the admin update endpoint, then fetches them and checks whether the information matches the last update. This ensures proper consistency and update propagation for frontend display.

dependencies.purpose: Admin updates the board settings to a known new value for verification of freshness on fetch.

scenario.draft: Test searching and paginating authentication tokens with a combination of valid filters such as actor_type, issued_at date range, and revoked status. The test should confirm that only tokens matching the search/filter criteria are returned and that pagination metadata is accurate. Precondition: ensure there exist tokens for multiple actor types (admin, member, moderator, guest) and different revoked statuses.

dependencies.purpose: Create several authentication tokens for different actor types and states to populate the dataset for search/filter scenarios.

scenario.draft: Test error handling when invalid or incorrectly formatted search/filter criteria are provided (e.g., malformed UUID, unsupported actor_type value). The API should return a meaningful validation error and must not expose sensitive operational details.

Test the ability to retrieve authentication tokens in multiple pages, ensuring sorting works as requested (e.g., by issued_at descending or ascending). The test should verify that results are consistent over navigated pages and sorting order.

dependencies.purpose: Create enough authentication tokens to require at least two pages of data when using default or minimal page sizes.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving the details of a specific authentication token by a valid UUID. The response should include all non-sensitive fields for the token and match data previously created. Precondition: create at least one valid authentication token and use its generated ID in the test.

dependencies.purpose: Create a valid authentication token and use its ID for retrieval.

scenario.draft: Test requesting authentication token details using an invalid or non-existent UUID. The test should verify that a 404 Not Found or appropriate error is returned and that no sensitive information is leaked in the error message.

Test successful creation of an authentication token using valid actor_type and actor_id. The resulting response should include all expected fields (omitting the raw token string if policy requires). Precondition: there must be a valid actor (e.g., admin, member, moderator, or guest) to assign as the token's owner.

Test attempt to create an authentication token with a token value that already exists (if uniqueness is enforced on the token string). Expect the API to reject the request and return an error indicating duplicate token violation.

dependencies.purpose: Create an initial authentication token with a specific token value to ensure the subsequent duplicate attempt triggers a conflict.

scenario.draft: Test creation attempt using a non-existent or invalid actor_id (e.g., non-UUID format or referencing a deleted user). The API should return a validation or not-found error and no token is created.

Test successfully revoking an authentication token by updating the revoked status. The response should show the token as revoked and unexpired (if not expired already). Precondition: a valid non-revoked token must exist to be updated.

dependencies.purpose: Create a valid, non-revoked authentication token to be updated during the test.

scenario.draft: Test updating a non-existent or invalid authentication token ID. The API should return a 404 or appropriate error indicating the target was not found and no update occurs.
Test updating a token with invalid or empty fields (e.g., expiration in the past, revoked with invalid value, etc.). The API should reject the update and return detailed validation errors.

dependencies.purpose: Create an authentication token to attempt an invalid update scenario (such as setting an already-expired date).

scenario.draft: Test successfully deleting an authentication token by its valid ID. After deletion, the token should no longer be retrievable via GET, and the operation should be irrevocable. Precondition: create a valid authentication token for deletion.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new authentication token whose ID will be used for the deletion test.

scenario.draft: Test attempting to delete a token with an invalid or non-existent UUID. Expect a meaningful error code (typically 404 Not Found) with no side effects or sensitive data exposure.

Test successful retrieval of all notification settings for an authenticated admin user. The test should verify that only the admin's own notification settings are returned, with delivery and category preferences present for each record. Pagination should be validated for larger result sets. All returned records must be properly scoped to the admin's user ID, and access should be denied for non-privileged users (covered in separate scenario).

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin account for authentication and authorization context.

scenario.draft: Verify that an admin cannot retrieve notification settings for other users by attempting the endpoint as a different admin, moderator, member, or guest. Only the authenticated user's own notification settings should be accessible. An attempt to access another user’s settings should be forbidden or return an empty result set, as appropriate.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin account for authentication and authorization context.
Create a moderator account for testing cross-role access restrictions.
Create a member account for testing access restrictions.

scenario.draft: Test that a moderator can retrieve all their own notification settings, with each entry containing proper delivery and category preferences. The test should cover the correct scoping of results to the authenticated moderator and validation of pagination. Attempting to access settings for any other user must not be allowed or must return no results (privacy enforcement).

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderator account for authentication and authorization context.

scenario.draft: Test that non-moderator users (members, guests) cannot access notification settings through the moderator endpoint. Attempting to access this endpoint as a non-moderator should result in access forbidden or an authentication error, ensuring enforcement of role-based access control.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account (non-moderator) for negative access test.

scenario.draft: Test that a member can retrieve all of their own notification settings, ensuring that delivery and category preferences are returned as per the schema. The test must validate that only the current member’s settings are shown and that pagination metadata is accurate when result sets are large.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account to prepare the user context for notification settings retrieval.

scenario.draft: Test the scenario where a member account is deactivated or not active. The member should not be able to retrieve notification settings after deactivation, and the API should return an authentication or access error as per business logic.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account.
Deactivate or set the 'is_active' flag to false for the test member account.

scenario.draft: Test that a guest (unauthenticated, session-based user) can access their own notification settings when a valid guest session is established. The test should verify that only the current guest’s notification settings are returned and that settings are properly initialized during guest onboarding. Edge cases include expired sessions or no settings configured, in which case the result should be empty or a valid notification settings structure with default values.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new guest session by registering a guest access record for the test context.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can filter their notification settings by specific categories (e.g., moderation, reply, vote) using the search endpoint. The test should check for accurate filtering and pagination. The request should include diverse setting entries for the admin and attempt a filtered search, verifying that only matching records are returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin account to configure multiple notification settings of different categories for search testing.
Create several notification settings entries with varying categories for the admin account.

scenario.draft: Test for correct error handling when the admin sends an invalid filter or search query (such as non-existent category values, malformed request body, or date parameters in the wrong format). The API should return relevant validation errors, not internal errors or unhelpful failure codes.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin account to submit search requests with intentionally invalid or malformed parameters.

scenario.draft: Test that a moderator can search and filter their notification settings using various advanced parameters such as delivery channel (in-app/email), category toggles (like moderation, reply, vote), and time ranges. Ensure search returns only the notification settings relevant to the authenticated moderator. Validate that pagination and sorting work as expected. Prepare by creating/modifying a variety of notification settings for the moderator via the relevant creation endpoint.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple notification settings records for the moderator, each with different delivery channels and categories to enable realistic search coverage.

scenario.draft: Verify that access to search notification settings with advanced parameters is denied if the user is not authenticated as a moderator or above. Try searching as a guest or member and expect a permission error, confirming role-based access is enforced for this moderator endpoint.

Verify that a member can search and filter their own notification settings using advanced parameters such as delivery channel, category toggles, and time ranges. Results should only include this member's records and be properly paginated/sorted. Pre-create multiple settings via the member notification settings creation endpoint for test coverage.

dependencies.purpose: Create several notification settings for the same member with different filter combinations to verify search responses include all and only their own records.

scenario.draft: Check that an unauthenticated or unauthorized request to this endpoint is denied with an appropriate error. Attempt to use the endpoint as a guest or a different member and ensure permission rules are correctly enforced so members can't search other users' notification settings.

Confirm a guest may search and filter their notification settings using allowed parameters such as delivery type, notification category, or time range. The results must only reflect the settings for the authenticated guest session. Ensure advanced queries cannot return or access other guests’ or members’ settings. Precondition: Register a guest notification setting and additional guest sessions if needed for testing cross-session security.

dependencies.purpose: Create one or more notification settings for the active guest session and optionally others to test isolation between sessions.

scenario.draft: Test that a guest attempting to search notification settings of a different guest session or of a member, moderator, or admin receives access denied or empty results, ensuring privacy and RBAC are enforced in the endpoint.

Test that an admin can retrieve the full details of a notification settings record they own by providing the notificationSettingId. Verify correct details are returned for the authenticated admin and that all preference fields (delivery channels, per-category toggles) are reflected accurately. Create such a settings record for the admin beforehand and use its ID for the GET request.

dependencies.purpose: Create a notification settings record for the admin user so that its ID can be used for the GET detail test.

scenario.draft: Ensure that if an admin user attempts to retrieve a notification settings record not owned by them (for example, a member's or different admin's settings), the endpoint returns a forbidden or not found error, upholding privacy and data access controls. Attempt GET with the ID of a notification setting belonging to another user type or admin and check the error response.

dependencies.purpose: Create a notification settings record for a member; use its ID to simulate cross-user/admin unauthorized GET attempts.

scenario.draft: Test that a moderator can retrieve their own notification settings using the notificationSettingId, verifying the response contains all preference fields and delivery configurations as expected. A pre-existing settings record for the moderator is needed; create one before running the GET call.

dependencies.purpose: Create a notification settings record for the moderator so that it can be fetched by get detail.

scenario.draft: Test that a moderator cannot access the detail of another user's notification setting, such as a member’s or another moderator’s. Attempt to GET a notificationSettingId belonging to a different user and verify the endpoint denies this access with the correct error or null result.

dependencies.purpose: Create a notification setting for a member to use its ID for unauthorized access attempt by the moderator.

scenario.draft: Test admin notification creation with fully valid input. Log in as an admin. Submit a creation request with all required fields, including a valid recipient (e.g., a member's ID or an admin's own ID), a notification message, correct category/type, and correct references. Verify that the notification is not only created but also linked to the appropriate recipient and visible in their notification inbox. Expected: 201 Created, notification appears for the intended recipient.

Test failure to create notification when required fields are missing. Log in as an admin. Attempt to create a notification while omitting mandatory fields (e.g., message, recipient ID, or category). The API should reject the request and return validation errors indicating which fields are missing. Expected: 400 Bad Request with error details.

Validate business error handling for notification creation when the recipient (admin_id, moderator_id, member_id, or guest_id) does not exist or is deactivated. Log in as admin, try to create a notification for a nonexistent or deactivated recipient. The API should respond with an error indicating recipient not found or not active. Expected: 404 Not Found or 422 Unprocessable Entity with error reason.

Test logic that prevents duplicate notifications for the same event to the same recipient if business logic requires deduplication. Simulate creating a notification for a recipient for a specific event, then attempt to create the exact notification again. If deduplication or idempotency is enforced, the system should block the duplicate or return relevant status. Expected: Either an error or status indicating duplication logic as implemented.

Test successful notification creation by a moderator for a valid recipient (admin, moderator, member, or guest). Verify that all mandatory fields are present and the new notification is visible to the intended recipient. Expected: 201 Created, notification delivered and shown in recipient's notification list.

Attempt to create a notification as moderator while omitting one or more required fields (such as recipient or message). API should reject the request and provide a clear validation error. Expected: 400 Bad Request with error message indicating missing fields.

Try to send a notification to a non-existent or inactive recipient (admin, moderator, member, or guest). The system should reject the request, indicating the recipient does not exist or is inactive. Expected: 404 Not Found or 422 Unprocessable Entity with clear explanation.

Test marking a notification as read via update by the admin. Authenticate as the admin. Update a notification (using a valid notificationId owned by the admin) to set its 'is_read' field to true. Confirm that the notification's state is updated only for the correct admin and that the change is persisted. Expected: 200 OK, notification is marked as read in the admin's list.

dependencies.purpose: First, create a notification to get a valid notificationId for update.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update a notification with a non-existent or unauthorized notificationId as admin. The API should return an error indicating the notification was not found or access is forbidden. Expected: 404 Not Found or 403 Forbidden.

Attempt to update immutable or restricted fields in a notification (e.g., attempt to change recipient or non-updatable metadata). The API should reject such updates to ensure business rules and data integrity. Expected: 400 Bad Request or 422 Unprocessable Entity with appropriate error details.

dependencies.purpose: Create a notification first so there is a target notification to update.

scenario.draft: Test moderator marking their own notification as read. As an authenticated moderator, update an owned notification using its notificationId to set 'is_read' to true. Confirm that the updated status is only reflected for this moderator's view. Expected: 200 OK and notification is now "read".

dependencies.purpose: Create a notification for the moderator to generate a valid notificationId.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update a notification as moderator, referencing an invalid or non-existent notificationId. Expected: 404 Not Found or 403 Forbidden as appropriate, verifying secure resource access.

Attempt to update a notification not intended for the current moderator, testing access control logic. The API should reject access or silently disallow update so that only the rightful recipient or privileged actor can change notification state. Expected: 403 Forbidden or similar.

dependencies.purpose: Create a notification for a different admin or recipient to test access control.

scenario.draft: Test member updating their own notification to mark it as read. As a logged-in member, update notificationId with 'is_read: true'. Confirm the change is accepted and only affects that member's inbox. Expected: 200 OK, notification marked as read.

dependencies.purpose: Admin creates a notification for the member account to set up a valid notificationId for the member to update.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update a notification using a notificationId that does not exist, as a member. The response should be a 404 Not Found, and no notification is updated.

Attempt by a member to update a notification addressed to a different user (admin, moderator, or another member). This should be rejected to enforce RBAC and data privacy. Expected: 403 Forbidden or 404 Not Found.

dependencies.purpose: Create a notification for another user (different member or moderator) to test access restriction.

scenario.draft: As a moderator, search for comments using common filtering criteria such as keywords in the body, member ID, post ID, and date ranges. Confirm results paginate correctly and reflect only permitted comment visibility according to moderator role (including soft-deleted if policy allows).

dependencies.purpose: Create sample comments with diverse bodies, members, posts, and timestamps to populate data for search and filtering tests.

scenario.draft: Use advanced search filters to retrieve only comments under a specific parent comment, verifying threaded conversations' correct hierarchical retrieval in the backend for moderation review. Paged results must match thread depth and filter constraints set in the request.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple comments with explicit parent-child relationships to form threaded comment trees for search testing.

scenario.draft: Verify that, as a moderator, soft-deleted comments (comments with deleted_at set) are returned when searching with appropriate filters. Ensure that RBAC correctly exposes these to moderators but not to ordinary members. Confirm that deleted comments are labeled appropriately in the response.

dependencies.purpose: Create comments, then soft-delete selected ones to create a test set that includes both active and deleted comments.
Soft-delete specific comments as setup, using their IDs from previous creations for later search verification.

scenario.draft: Attempt a comment search as moderator with invalid filter criteria, such as an improperly formatted date, excessively large page size, or a non-existent member ID. Confirm the system returns a clear validation error and does not process the query.

As an admin, perform an advanced search over comments using multiple filters jointly (body content, author member ID, post ID, date ranges, and parent ID). Validate that paginated results match all search parameters and show both regular and soft-deleted comments according to RBAC.

dependencies.purpose: Create a collection of comments with varied content, parent-child structure, authors, and posts to facilitate comprehensive search scenarios.

scenario.draft: Conduct a search as admin with filter criteria guaranteed not to match any existing comments (e.g., nonsensical body text, non-existent member ID). Ensure that an empty result set and correct pagination metadata are returned.

Attempt to search comments with a page size exceeding the maximum allowed by system configuration. Verify that the API correctly returns an error indicating invalid page size, enforcing pagination limits.

A logged-in member retrieves the full details of a comment they authored. Confirm all fields—including content, author info, post linkage, parent-child references, timestamps, and absence of deleted_at for active comments—are correctly returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new comment authored by the member to ensure its existence for retrieval.

scenario.draft: A member retrieves a comment made by another member on a public post. Confirm that the full details are returned, provided the requesting user has permission to view the post and comment.

dependencies.purpose: Create a public post authored by one member.
Create a comment on the public post by a different member.

scenario.draft: A member attempts to fetch details of a comment on a post they do not have access to (e.g., private post) or one that has been soft-deleted. The system should return a forbidden/not found error and not leak data about the restricted or deleted comment.

dependencies.purpose: Create a private post or a post the member cannot access.
Create a comment under the private post.
Soft-delete another comment for the same scenario group.

scenario.draft: A moderator retrieves the full details of a comment, including comments that have been soft-deleted (deleted_at set). Confirm that all fields, including deletion info, are populated for moderator audit and review.

dependencies.purpose: Create one or more comments.
Soft-delete a target comment to verify retrieval of deleted status by moderator.

scenario.draft: As a moderator, fetch the details of a comment that resides in a post or thread restricted from regular member access (e.g., in a private or moderated section). Confirm that moderators are granted access and all comment detail fields are present.

dependencies.purpose: Create a private/moderated post with restricted access.
Add a comment to the restricted post.

scenario.draft: Admin retrieves the full details of any comment, including those soft-deleted or on private posts. Confirm the API returns all atomic schema fields, deleted_at (if any), and relationships for legal or compliance audits.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment as a regular member.
Soft-delete that comment to test admin retrieval.

scenario.draft: As admin, attempt to retrieve a comment with a non-existing or improperly formatted UUID. Confirm the API returns a not found or validation error, never leaking comment existence details for security compliance.

Test retrieving the detailed profile of a specific member as a moderator when the member exists. First, create a member account to ensure there is a valid memberId. Then, as an authenticated moderator, attempt to fetch the details of that member. The expected outcome is that the full profile, including administrative and audit fields, is returned with no sensitive information (like password hash), and the operation succeeds for authorized roles.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member so as to have a valid memberId to query for.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving member details as a moderator when the specified memberId does not exist. As an authenticated moderator, attempt to fetch details for a non-existent or randomly generated member UUID. The expected outcome is that the endpoint returns an appropriate 404 error or not found response, verifying error handling for invalid member references.

Test attempting to retrieve member details as a non-privileged user or using an invalid/expired session. Attempt to fetch details as a user without moderator/admin privileges or with no authentication. The expected outcome is an authentication or authorization error, verifying strict RBAC enforcement.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member, if needed, to avoid false negatives on nonexistence errors.

scenario.draft: Test successful registration of a new member using valid display name, email, and a strong password that meets business policy. Submit the registration request as a guest (unauthenticated). Expected outcome is a successful creation response containing the new member's full profile, proper initialization of verification and status fields, and audit timestamps.

Test member registration failure due to using an email address that already exists in the system. First, create an initial member with a specific unique email. Then, attempt to register another member using the same email. The expected outcome is a validation error indicating email uniqueness violation and failure to create the account.

dependencies.purpose: Create the first member with the given email to enforce uniqueness check for the second registration.

scenario.draft: Test failure when registering a new member with an invalid email format in the registration payload. Submit a request with an email not conforming to standard email format. Expected outcome is a validation error indicating improper formatting and no member account created.

Test failure when attempting to create a new member with a weak password that does not meet system strength requirements. Submit the registration with a too-short or commonly used password. Expect validation error, with details specifying the password policy violation, and no account is created.

Test successful updating of a member's profile by an admin. First, create a member, then as an admin, update editable fields such as display name or verification status. The expected outcome is that the member's profile is updated, audit logs are adjusted, and all changes are reflected in the response. Only permitted fields should be updatable, and business logic such as email uniqueness must be enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new member to use in update scenario.

scenario.draft: Test failure when an admin tries updating a member's email address to one already in use by another member. First, create two members with unique emails. As an admin, attempt to update the second member's email to match the first. The expected outcome is a validation error specifying the uniqueness violation.

dependencies.purpose: Create the first member with a unique email.
Create the second member whose email will be updated to a duplicate.

scenario.draft: Test updating a member profile with invalid data (e.g., invalid email format, weak password, or restricted field modifications) as an admin. The expected result is a detailed error message for the specific violation (invalid email format, weak password, or unmodifiable field), and the original member information remains unchanged.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member for testing invalid update scenarios.

scenario.draft: Test that a logged-in member can successfully update their own profile fields, such as display name or password, following proper authentication. Create a member account, log in as that member, and submit a valid update. The expected outcome is a successful profile update and confirmation in the response.

dependencies.purpose: Create the member who will perform self-update.

scenario.draft: Test that a member attempting to update their email to an invalid format receives a validation error and that the profile is not updated. Validate that detailed feedback is given and audit logs reflect the attempted change.

dependencies.purpose: Create the member for the scenario.

scenario.draft: Test a member attempting to update another member's profile (not their own), which should fail due to insufficient permissions. Validate that the system enforces ownership and returns an authorization error, leaving data unchanged.

dependencies.purpose: Create at least two member accounts: one as the actor and one as the target of the update.

scenario.draft: Test successful permanent deletion of a member by an admin. First, create a new member, then as an admin, perform the delete operation using the member's ID. Confirm the member is no longer retrievable and all associations are properly handled or cascaded as per business logic.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new member to be deleted.

scenario.draft: Test deletion of a non-existent member by an admin. Attempt to delete a memberId that does not exist. The expected result is an appropriate not found error (404) or business rule violation message, and data integrity is maintained.

Test attempting to delete a member without admin privileges or using an invalid/expired token. Attempt the deletion as a non-admin account or unauthenticated session. The expected result is an authorization error and no member data is deleted.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member to use as the target for unauthorized deletion.

scenario.draft: Test the ability for a guest user to mark a notification as read through this endpoint. Begin by ensuring a guest session exists and at least one notification, addressed to this session, has been delivered (using notification creation endpoints or guest actions that would trigger notifications). Attempt to update the notification with the is_read property set to true, and verify the read status is updated. Ensure that the guest session has the correct notificationId and proper authentication token/session if required.

dependencies.purpose: Register a guest session to obtain a guestId required for notification assignment and identification.
Create and deliver a notification to the guest user so there is a real notificationId to update.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update a notification as a guest for which the current session is NOT the recipient. This should return a forbidden or unauthorized error, ensuring guests can only alter their own notifications. Set up by creating a guest and issuing notifications to multiple guestIds, then have one guest attempt to update another's notificationId.

dependencies.purpose: Register two separate guest sessions (A and B), both with their own guestIds, to create isolation of guest resources.
Create notifications, assigning one to guest A and another to guest B, to be able to test cross-guest update attempt.

scenario.draft: Verify that an admin user can successfully delete their own notification by notificationId. First, ensure an admin account exists and a notification is issued to this admin (either by system action or via notification creation endpoint). Then invoke the delete operation and confirm that the notification is removed and no longer accessible to the admin, checking that all schema-side references are properly cleaned up.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin account to act as the recipient of the notification.
Deliver a notification specifically addressed to the new admin and retrieve the notificationId for deletion.

scenario.draft: Attempt to delete a notification as an admin, where the notification belongs to another user (e.g., another admin, moderator, member, or guest). The operation should be forbidden and must return a proper error code/status. The test should create notifications for multiple users and attempt cross-user deletion to ensure RBAC integrity.

dependencies.purpose: Create two admin accounts, each able to independently receive notifications.
Issue separate notifications to each admin (or other users/roles, such as moderators/members/guests).

scenario.draft: Test that a moderator can successfully delete their own notification. Create a moderator account, send a notification to this moderator, and then delete it, verifying its removal from the system and confirming its inaccessibility after deletion.

dependencies.purpose: Register a moderator who will be the notification recipient.
Send a notification to the newly created moderator to set up test deletion.

scenario.draft: Ensure that a moderator cannot delete a notification that belongs to a different user (another moderator, admin, member, or guest). Attempting this should result in a forbidden or unauthorized error. Set up two users (moderators or other roles), issue notifications to each, and attempt a cross-user deletion.

dependencies.purpose: Register two moderator accounts for independent notification assignment.
Send notifications targeted to each moderator (or other roles for wider cross-role testing).

scenario.draft: Verify that a member can delete notifications addressed to them. Register a member, send a notification to this member, perform the delete operation, and confirm the notification is no longer accessible.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new member who will receive test notifications.
Create and deliver a notification to the member, acquiring the notificationId for deletion.

scenario.draft: Attempt to delete a notification as a member where the notificationId is assigned to a different member. This should return a forbidden/unauthorized error and leave the other member's notification untouched. Register two members, assign notifications, and perform a cross-user deletion attempt.

dependencies.purpose: Create two members for isolated resource ownership (member A and member B).
Deliver notifications to both members, allowing for attempted cross-member deletion.

scenario.draft: Confirm that a guest user can delete their own notification. First, create a guest session and assign a notification to that guest. Perform the delete and verify that the notification is permanently removed, validating guest-specific RBAC policies.

dependencies.purpose: Initiate a guest session and get a guestId for notification addressing.
Issue a notification to the guest session, obtaining its notificationId for subsequent deletion.

scenario.draft: Check that a guest cannot delete another guest's notification. With two guest sessions created, each with notifications, have one guest attempt to delete a notification belonging to the other. The system should reject the action with a forbidden or unauthorized error, maintaining data privacy and role isolation.

dependencies.purpose: Create two distinct guest sessions with unique guestIds.
Send notifications to each guest separately, so that guest A can attempt to delete guest B's notification (and expect an error).

scenario.draft: Test the ability of a moderator to delete a specific post vote by its ID. First, create a member, a moderator, and a post as the member. Then, cast a vote on the post as the member. Finally, as the moderator, delete the vote using this endpoint and verify that the vote is removed from the database. Ensure audit logs reflect the deletion action.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post as a member so there is a post to vote on.
Cast a vote on the post as the member to generate a post vote that can be deleted.

scenario.draft: Test error handling when an attempt is made to delete a post vote with a non-existent or invalid postVoteId. As a moderator, use a valid postId but an invalid or random UUID for postVoteId, and verify that the system returns a not found error and logs the attempt for audit purposes.

Test that non-moderators (such as a member) cannot delete a post vote using the moderator endpoint. After creating a post and a vote as a member, have the member attempt to delete the vote via this endpoint, and verify that an authorization error is returned and no deletion occurs.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post as a member so there is a post to vote on.
Cast a vote on the post as the member to generate a post vote that an unauthorized user will attempt to delete.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can successfully delete a post vote. Create a member, admin, and post as the member. The member votes on the post. The admin then deletes the vote by this endpoint and validation checks that the vote is removed, and audit logs reflect the admin action.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post as a member for voting.
Cast the vote as the member to produce a deletable vote.

scenario.draft: Test the case when the admin attempts to delete a non-existent post vote. Supply a valid postId and a random UUID as postVoteId. The system must respond with a not found error and record the attempt in the audit trail.

Ensure RBAC prevents non-admin roles from deleting a post vote via the admin endpoint. After a member creates and votes on a post, attempt to delete the vote as a member or unauthorized role, and check for proper permission denial and retention of the vote.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post for the vote.
Record a member's vote to attempt unauthorized deletion by a non-admin.

scenario.draft: Test that an authenticated member can successfully retrieve the list of all votes for a specific comment. First, create a post and a comment on that post, then cast multiple votes (upvote and downvote) on the comment by various members. Use this endpoint as one of the voting members to fetch all votes for the comment and verify correct pagination and vote record structure, including upvote/downvote and voter data.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post to host the comment.
Create a comment on the post to be voted on.
Submit at least one upvote and one downvote from different members for the comment.

scenario.draft: Test behavior when trying to list votes for a commentId that does not exist. Attempt to fetch votes for a random UUID and verify that the API returns a not found error, with no data leakage.

Verify that an unauthenticated or unauthorized user (guest) is prevented from accessing the comment votes endpoint. Attempt to access this endpoint without authentication, expecting permission denied or 401/403 response code.

Test advanced search for comment votes using type and date range filters. After creating a post and comment, multiple members vote (both upvote and downvote) at different times. Use this endpoint with filters to fetch only upvotes or only downvotes, or votes cast within a certain time period, and check that results match the criteria.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post to allow comment creation.
Add a comment for voting.
Record votes from multiple members on the target comment at distinct times.

scenario.draft: Test the reaction of the endpoint to invalid search/filter criteria (e.g., invalid vote type, malformed parameters, or out-of-bounds dates). Ensure the API returns a validation error and does not expose internal data.

Ensure that an unauthorized or unauthenticated user cannot perform advanced searches for comment votes. Attempt to use this endpoint as a guest or without credentials and verify the rejection and no data exposure.

Verify a member can retrieve details of a specific comment vote by its ID. After creating a comment and voting as a member, use this endpoint to fetch the vote details and validate all relevant fields are returned (voter, type, timestamps).

dependencies.purpose: Create a post for the comment.
Create a comment to be voted on.
Cast a vote as the member and capture the vote ID for retrieval.

scenario.draft: Test the endpoint's response when requesting comment vote details for a non-existent or malformed commentVoteId. Ensure the system returns not found error and no sensitive info.

Test that guests and unauthorized users cannot retrieve details of a specific comment vote. Attempt to use this endpoint without valid member authentication, verifying permission denial with no data breach.

Verify that an admin can permanently delete a guest session record by supplying a valid guestId. Start by registering a new guest session so the ID is known, then perform the DELETE operation and confirm the session is removed from the database and cannot be retrieved afterwards. Also, validate that audit logs (if implemented elsewhere) reflect this action.

dependencies.purpose: To create a new guest session and obtain a guestId for deletion testing.

scenario.draft: Test that attempting to delete a guest session with a non-existent or already-deleted guestId results in a proper error response, such as 404 not found. Ensure no side effects are caused by this invalid deletion attempt.

Ensure that only users with admin privileges can perform guest record deletions. Attempt to delete a guest session as a non-admin (or unauthenticated) user and confirm access is denied with an appropriate error response (e.g., 403 Forbidden).

dependencies.purpose: To create a guest session and guarantee its presence for attempted unauthorized deletion.

scenario.draft: Validate that both guests and authenticated members can retrieve a paginated list of discussion board posts. Ensure only non-deleted posts are returned, and that the list adheres to privacy and category visibility (public/private) rules. Test both guest and member access to determine RBAC correctly affects results.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new member to test authenticated member access.

scenario.draft: Test the scenario in which there are no posts in the system or all posts are soft-deleted. Confirm that the response is an empty result set and that pagination metadata accurately reflects zero results.
Create posts and then soft-delete some of them. Verify the API does not include soft-deleted posts in the response while active posts remain visible. Validate for both guests and members.

dependencies.purpose: Create posts for testing (requires member creation).
Soft-delete published posts to confirm exclusion from listings.

scenario.draft: Verify that the advanced post search allows filtering posts by category, tag, and author. Create sample posts with different categories, tags, and authors, then perform a filtered search to confirm only matching posts are returned. Also ensure pagination and sorting options work as specified.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple posts with various categories, tags, and authors for search filtering.

scenario.draft: Ensure that posts which are soft-deleted do not appear in advanced search results. Create and soft-delete a post, then attempt to search for it with criteria that would normally match. Confirm the result does not include the soft-deleted post.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post for testing.
Soft-delete the post to set up exclusion from search.

scenario.draft: Submit a search request with malformed or logically invalid parameters (e.g., invalid UUIDs, unsupported filters, or out-of-bounds pagination). Verify the API returns validation errors and does not process the query.

Confirm that fetching post details with a valid, public postId returns all expected data, including author, categories, and tags. Ensure this works for both guests and members, and that only appropriate metadata is exposed per RBAC.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new post to get a valid postId for detail fetch.

scenario.draft: Attempt to retrieve post details using a non-existent or incorrectly-formatted postId. Verify that the API responds with an appropriate error such as 404 not found or validation error.

Test that attempting to fetch details for a post that has been soft-deleted does not return the post for normal users (guests, members), but may be retrievable by admins or moderators if permitted by policy.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post for testing.
Soft-delete the post to test restricted visibility in detail view.

scenario.draft: Verify that a member can successfully create a post by providing only the mandatory fields: author memberId, title, and body (with optional parent_id omitted). Confirm the post is created with correct metadata and appears in listings.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new member to create and own the post.

scenario.draft: Test that a member can create a new post and assign categories and tags if those fields are supported in the create schema. Ensure assignments are reflected in the response and listings, and related dependencies (categories, tags) must exist before assignment.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member to create the post.
Fetch available categories to assign to the post.
Fetch available tags to assign to the post.

scenario.draft: Attempt to create a post as an unauthenticated user (or with improper credentials). Confirm the API responds with an authorization or authentication error, preventing post creation.

Attempt to create a post with invalid data such as missing required fields, invalid memberId, or violating title/body constraints (e.g., excessively long strings, empty fields). Confirm validation errors are returned and no post is created.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member for use in testing invalid post creation scenarios.

scenario.draft: Test successful creation of a new tag by an admin, providing a unique label, a description, and a color. Confirm the response includes all metadata, and the new tag is available for selection/assignment.

Test failure when attempting to create a tag with a label that already exists in the discussion board tags table. First create a tag with a given label, then attempt to create another with the same label, expecting a uniqueness constraint violation error and a clear error message.

dependencies.purpose: Create the initial tag with a specific label to set up a duplicate label scenario.

scenario.draft: Test failure of tag creation when the required 'label' field is omitted from the request. Validation should fail, and the API must return an error indicating the missing required field.

Test successful retrieval of an existing tag's full details by its tagId. Ensure returned data matches the created tag's label, description, color, and metadata. The tag must already exist—set up by admin creation flow.

dependencies.purpose: Create a tag as setup, so its tagId can be used for retrieval.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval of a tag by a tagId that does not exist in the system. The API should return an appropriate not found (404) error response.

Test that a guest attempting to fetch a soft-deleted tag by tagId does not receive the tag details or receives a forbidden/not found error. The tag should be created, soft-deleted by admin, and then retrieved as guest.

dependencies.purpose: Create a tag for test initialization.
Soft-delete the tag to simulate a deleted state.

scenario.draft: Test successful update of a tag's label, description, or color by an admin. Create a tag first, then update its fields, and verify the response includes the updated values and audit metadata.

dependencies.purpose: Create the tag to be updated.

scenario.draft: Test failure when updating a tag's label to one that already exists on another tag. Create two distinct tags, then attempt to update the second's label to match the first's, expecting a uniqueness constraint error.

dependencies.purpose: Create the first tag with original label.
Create the second tag that will attempt a duplicate label on update.

scenario.draft: Test that updating a tag's color with an improperly formatted value (e.g., invalid hex code) results in a validation error. This confirms proper input validation for color fields.

dependencies.purpose: Create a tag for update scenario.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update a tag using a tagId that does not exist. Confirm that the API returns a 404 not found error response.
Test successful soft-deletion (deleted_at set) of an existing tag by an admin. Verify that the tag remains in the database but is no longer visible to regular users for assignment or selection.

dependencies.purpose: Create a tag to be soft-deleted.

scenario.draft: Test that deleting a tag which is already soft-deleted either returns idempotent success or a clear error indicating prior deletion, according to business policy. First create and delete the tag, then attempt to delete it again.

dependencies.purpose: Create tag to be deleted.
Execute the first soft-delete operation.

scenario.draft: Test deletion request using an invalid or malformed UUID as tagId. The API should return an appropriate validation or error response, confirming path parameter validation.

Test successful retrieval of the complete list of all category-tag assignments by an admin. Ensure the response includes valid assignment objects and that all created links between categories and tags are present. Use tag/category creation flows as needed to establish expected data.

dependencies.purpose: Create at least one tag to link to a category.
Create at least one category for assignment.
Assign the tag to the category to establish a category-tag assignment for the test.

scenario.draft: Test listing category-tag assignments when none exist in the database. Expect an empty array or appropriate empty paginated result.
Test that unauthenticated requests to retrieve all category-tag assignments are denied or do not return sensitive configuration data, verifying that proper authorization is enforced.

Test successful submission of a content abuse report by a member through the moderator endpoint. Start with an authenticated member who identifies a problematic post or comment, fills in valid reason, category, and references the affected content ID. The API should validate all references, store the report, and return the created report marked as pending or under_review. This scenario verifies correct validation, linkage to the reporter, and initial status assignment.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new member account to use as the reporting user.
Create a sample post to be reported by the member.

scenario.draft: Test failure response when attempting to report a non-existent or invalid post or comment via the moderator endpoint. An authenticated member uploads a report referencing an invalid content ID. The API should reject the report creation and respond with an appropriate error indicating invalid reference, without creating any new report entry.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account for reporting.

scenario.draft: Test that duplicate content abuse reports for the same content and reason cannot be submitted multiple times by the same member. First, register a member, create and report a specific post or comment, then attempt to report it again with the same reason and context. The API should return an error indicating a duplicate or already-existing report, enforcing idempotence and deduplication business rules.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account.
Create a post to be reported.
Submit the first report for deduplication testing.

scenario.draft: Verify that an admin can submit a content abuse report as part of a system escalation process (e.g., escalated from automated detection or cross-system flag). Begin with a valid admin, reference either an existing post or comment, specify escalation category and reason, and confirm that the report's status and audit fields are set appropriately for an admin-origin report. This is useful for platform abuse and compliance cases.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin account to submit the report.
Create a post to be reported by the admin for escalation testing.

scenario.draft: Check that submitting an abuse/content report with a category not recognized by system business rules results in an error and no report created. Admin attempts to use an invalid or deprecated category, which is rejected according to API's validation logic. Response must clearly indicate which field was invalid.

dependencies.purpose: Provide an admin user for the attempt.
Provide a post ID for reporting.

scenario.draft: Test that a guest user can submit a content abuse report. The scenario starts with an unauthenticated session, selects an existing post to report, and provides mandatory guest metadata such as session or IP if required. The API should accept the report with proper association to the guest record. The response should represent a pending moderation status and link the report to the guest, ensuring no privilege escalation.

dependencies.purpose: Register a guest access (session) for tracing the reporter.
Add a post for the guest to report.

scenario.draft: Confirm that an abuse report submitted by a guest referencing a non-existent or deleted post is rejected. The scenario simulates a guest session attempting to report invalid content. The API must respond with clear validation error messages and not create any moderation report for invalid references.

dependencies.purpose: Register a guest session to submit the report.

scenario.draft: Test that a moderator can update a moderation report to progress its workflow, such as changing status from pending to under_review or resolved and adding a rationale. Moderator should fetch an existing report, update allowed fields, and verify the response reflects the changes, maintaining audit compliance and workflow history.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new report for updating.

scenario.draft: Verify that the API rejects invalid status transitions of moderation reports according to business rules (e.g., moving from resolved back to pending). The scenario advances a report to resolved status, then attempts an illegal transition to a previous state, expecting the system to return an error and preserve state integrity.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new report for status progression.
Advance the report status to 'resolved' before testing invalid transition.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can update a content report by adding a resolution note, such as rationale for action taken or moderation feedback. This should be reflected in the report's audit log. Start with an existing report, perform the update as admin, and confirm the new rationale and timestamps are present in the updated report.

dependencies.purpose: Create a content report to update with a resolution note.

scenario.draft: Ensure that an attempt by an admin to update a moderation report using a disallowed or immutable field (such as manually altering the reporter or content reference) fails with an error, with the API returning a clear validation message and preserving the original report unmodified.

dependencies.purpose: Create a report for attempting an invalid update field.

scenario.draft: Verify that an admin user can successfully delete an access log entry by its unique accessLogId. First, create a valid admin account and log in to receive authentication. Attempt to delete this newly created log using its ID and verify the operation returns a successful response with the log removed from subsequent listings. This tests basic delete functionality for authorized admins.

Create a new access log entry to ensure there is a valid log record to delete.

scenario.draft: Test the system's behavior when an admin attempts to delete a non-existent access log entry. scenario.draft: Ensure that non-admin users, such as moderators, members, or guests, cannot delete access logs. Register a guest session to simulate non-admin deletion attempts.

scenario.draft: Test a moderator submitting a new appeal for a specific moderation action. Validate that the appeal is accepted, properly linked to both the member and action, and returned with a pending status for further review.

Record a moderation action involving the test member, which can then be appealed.

scenario.draft: Test the system's enforcement of required fields by attempting to submit an appeal as a member without providing a reason. The API should reject the request with a validation error explaining that the reason is required, and ensure no appeal is created.

scenario.draft: Attempt to appeal a moderation action that has already been resolved and marked as final. Update the moderation action status to a resolved or closed state before testing appeal rejection.

scenario.draft: Test submitting an appeal as a guest omitting or providing invalid actor/session identifying information that is mandatory for guest actions. The server should reject the appeal and return a clear error about missing required guest actor identification with no side effects.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderation action that could be subject to a guest appeal.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can update the status of an existing appeal from pending to approved, along with providing an appropriate rationale for the decision. Validate that the update is reflected correctly in the appeal record and that audit/compliance logging occurs.

scenario.draft: Test the behavior when an admin attempts to update an appeal that does not exist. Attempt to PUT an update on a non-existent appealId and verify that the server returns a suitable error indicating the appeal was not found, and that no unexpected changes occur in the system.

dependencies.purpose: Create a pending appeal to be updated by the moderator.

scenario.draft: Test that an attempt by a moderator to update an appeal with an invalid status value (not allowed by system enum) is rejected. Attempt to PUT an invalid status update and verify that the API validates status values strictly and returns an error without modifying the appeal record.

Initial soft-delete of the post.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member for posting and commenting.
Create a discussion board post (to get postId).
Create multiple comments on the post, as a member.

scenario.draft: Test fetching the comment list for a post that currently has no comments. Create a post as a member but do not add comments, then call this endpoint and verify the response contains an empty list with correct metadata.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member.
Create a post to get a postId.

scenario.draft: Test that comments with deleted_at set are excluded from the list for general users. Create and then soft-delete a comment, then ensure it does not appear in the list from this endpoint. Moderators/admin scenarios can be separate.

Create a post to comment on.
Create at least two comments on the post.
Soft-delete one of the comments to test exclusion in results.

Add several comments.
Soft-delete at least one comment.

scenario.draft: Test that the endpoint correctly returns a validation error when given bad search criteria (such as invalid page size, unsupported filter values, or malformed query data). Send an invalid request body and verify that the response describes the validation issue.

Test retrieving details for a valid comment by postId and commentId. Set up a post and comment as preconditions, then call this endpoint and verify that the response includes all expected fields, author, and threading info.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member.

Create a comment for lookup.

scenario.draft: Test the endpoint's response when the commentId does not exist for a valid postId. Attempt to fetch a random or deleted comment and expect the API to return a 404 or not-found error.

Create a post for reference.

scenario.draft: Test for the edge case where a valid commentId is provided, but the postId in the path does not own that comment. Attempt to retrieve the comment with a mismatched postId and verify that the system returns an appropriate linkage or not-found error.

Create at least two posts.
Create a comment on the first post.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member account for commenting.
Create a post to comment on.

scenario.draft: Test the scenario where a member attempts to create a comment on a postId that does not exist. Use an invalid UUID for postId and verify that the system returns a not-found or error response indicating the post does not exist.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member account for posting and commenting.

scenario.draft: Test that a comment cannot be created by an unauthenticated user. Attempt to post a comment as a guest or without authentication and verify that the system returns an unauthorized/access denied error.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post as a member first, so there is a valid postId for commenting.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new verified member to act as the post author.

It verifies: 1) expected appeals are returned based on filters; 2) pagination and count are correct; 3) error is returned if invalid filter is used. The business value is compliance, workflow efficiency, and data integrity for high-volume or regulatory review.

This scenario ensures data integrity, workflow compliance, and error transparency.
